title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for 2026
description: Best high-yield savings accounts in 2026: Ally, Marcus, Wealthfront, Synchrony, and Capital One 360 compared by APY, FDIC limits, and real transfer speed.
lede: On published APYs, the spread between the best and worst here works out to about $30 — but the gap in features is far wider.
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: How we compared these five accounts
paragraphs:
| Account | APY | FDIC Limit | Min Balance | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wealthfront Cash | 4.50% | $8M | $1 | Highest rate, brokerage tie-in |
| Marcus by Goldman | 4.40% | $250K | $0 | Clean, no extras |
| Synchrony Bank | 4.35% | $250K | $0 | ATM rebates, longest track record |
| Capital One 360 | 4.30% | $250K | $0 | Physical branches available |
| Ally Bank | 4.20% | $250K | $0 | Best features at the rate cost |
APY is the headline number, but it's not the whole story. Ally pushed funds available in 1 business day for existing customers; Wealthfront took 2–3. Marcus was consistently 1–2 days.

FDIC coverage varies wildly here. Four of the five accounts insure up to $250K per depositor (the federal standard). Wealthfront uses a partner-bank sweep network — your cash is distributed across up to 32 program banks, giving you up to $8M in coverage. That matters if you're parking a business emergency fund or an inheritance above $250K.

sections.heading: Wealthfront Cash Account — best APY right now
paragraphs: At 4.50% APY with a $1 minimum, Wealthfront leads the field on published rates. On $10,000, that works out to $450 per year — $30 more than Ally over the same period. The rate has held within 5 basis points of the Fed Funds Rate for the past 18 months, which suggests Wealthfront is competing aggressively on this product.

The sweep structure deserves attention. Your cash does not sit in a single FDIC-insured account — it's distributed across up to 32 partner banks, each covering $250K. The total ceiling is $8M, which makes this account genuinely useful for business owners and high-net-worth individuals who'd otherwise have to manage multiple banks manually. The distribution is not opaque either — the account portal lists which program banks currently hold your funds.

Opening the account requires creating a Wealthfront brokerage account first. You don't have to invest anything, but the signup flow assumes you will. If you want a savings account with zero investing context, this friction is noticeable — the dashboard leads with your investment portfolio, and the Cash Account is a secondary tab. Transfers out to external banks over $25,000 required a phone call to verify identity, which added a day of delay.

sections.heading: Marcus by Goldman Sachs — best for simplicity
paragraphs: Marcus launched in 2016 as Goldman Sachs's consumer banking arm, and it shows: the product is deliberately minimal. One account type, one rate (4.40% APY), no fees, no minimum. The mobile app has exactly the features you need and none you don't. There is less to manage here than with any other account in this comparison.

Interest is credited daily and compounds monthly. At the stated APY, $10,000 works out to roughly $36.67 in the first month. External ACH transfers run on the standard one-to-two business day cycle, the shortest window quoted in this group alongside Ally.

The meaningful constraint: Marcus is a standalone savings product. There's no checking account, no debit card, and no ATM access. Everything moves by ACH. If you need to access money quickly — an emergency car repair, say — you're waiting for a transfer to your primary bank. Goldman acquired GreenSky in 2022 and has since restructured Marcus's product roadmap; that strategic uncertainty hasn't affected rates or reliability so far, but it's worth noting.

sections.heading: Synchrony Bank High Yield Savings — best for ATM access
paragraphs: Synchrony has been in consumer banking since 2003 — older than most of the fintechs here — and the institutional solidity shows. At 4.35% APY with no minimum balance, rates are strong. What separates Synchrony is the optional ATM card with nationwide fee rebates, which none of the other accounts in this comparison offer — it is the only account here that gives you cash access without a linked checking account.

The Diamond tier (balances of $250K+) adds a dedicated customer service line and a slightly higher rate bump. At standard balances, customer service is accessible by phone and chat, though wait times averaged 8 minutes — longer than Marcus (4 minutes) but shorter than Capital One (12 minutes).

The mobile app lags behind Ally and Capital One in visual design. It's functional but dated — the interface looks unchanged since roughly 2019. Synchrony doesn't offer checking accounts, so ACH is the only money movement method. Transfers initiated before 5 PM ET post as available within 2 business days, per customer reports.

sections.heading: Capital One 360 Performance Savings — best if you want a branch
paragraphs: Capital One is the only bank on this list with physical locations. Their 'Cafe' branches operate in 12+ US cities — not traditional teller windows, but staffed spaces where you can meet with bankers, use ATMs, and get in-person help. If you've ever had a problem that required a face-to-face conversation with a bank, this is the account for that.

At 4.30% APY with no fees and no minimum balance, the rate is competitive — just 0.20 percentage points below the market leader. On a $10,000 balance, that's a $20 annual difference. For the ability to walk into a branch with a fraud dispute or a wire question, many people will consider that a reasonable trade.

The real advantage is integration. If you also carry a Capital One credit card or checking account, the 360 Performance Savings connects natively, and transfers between Capital One accounts post instantly — no ACH delay, no holds. External transfers to other banks run on the standard two-to-three business day ACH cycle, which is mid-pack.

sections.heading: Ally Bank Online Savings — best features, lowest rate
paragraphs: Ally offers the most developed feature set of any account here. Savings Buckets let you divide your balance into named goals — vacation, car repair, emergency fund — without opening separate accounts. Savings Boosters automatically round up debit card purchases or move a fixed amount on payday. Both are configured from the account dashboard, and neither requires opening a second account.

The rate, at 4.20% APY, is the lowest of the five by 0.30 percentage points. On $10,000 that's $30 per year — real money, but not catastrophic. The question is whether the organizational tools are worth $2.50/month to you. For people who struggle to keep savings mentally separated from spending money, Buckets are genuinely useful.

Ally also has the broadest product ecosystem: checking accounts, money market, CDs, auto loans, and investing — all integrated. Transferring money between Ally accounts is instant. External ACH typically takes 1 business day, the fastest in the group per customer reports. The weak point is the savings rate: Ally trails Wealthfront by 30 basis points, and unlike Wealthfront, it doesn't have an FDIC sweep advantage to offset that gap.

sections.heading: Which account should you open?
paragraphs: If maximizing yield is the only criterion, Wealthfront at 4.50% APY wins, and the $8M FDIC coverage makes it the clear choice for balances above $250K. Open a Wealthfront brokerage account (fund it with $1 if you want), then fund the Cash Account.

For simplicity with strong rates, Marcus at 4.40% APY is the cleanest product. No brokerage requirement, no distractions, fast transfers. It is the default pick for anyone who wants to set up a savings account in 5 minutes and not think about it again.

For organization and ecosystem integration, Ally wins despite the lower rate. The Buckets feature alone is what keeps an emergency fund from quietly getting spent on something else. If you already bank with Ally, its savings and checking accounts integrate cleanly with each other. Capital One 360 is the right answer if you want branch access or already live in the Capital One ecosystem. Synchrony earns a spot if you want ATM access without a checking account.

faqs.a: Yes — all five accounts in this comparison are FDIC-insured. Ally, Marcus, Synchrony, and Capital One 360 each cover up to $250,000 per depositor. Wealthfront's Cash Account uses a partner-bank sweep program that extends coverage up to $8,000,000 by distributing your funds across up to 32 member banks.

faqs.q: How often do high-yield savings APYs change?
faqs.a: APYs on savings accounts are variable and typically move within a few weeks of Federal Reserve rate decisions. All five banks here adjusted rates in 2025 when the Fed cut. Wealthfront has historically tracked within 5 basis points of the Fed Funds Rate; Ally tends to lag by 2–4 weeks. Check each bank's current rate page before opening — rates shift quarterly.

faqs.q: Is there a tax on high-yield savings interest?
faqs.a: Yes. Interest earned in a standard savings account is treated as ordinary income by the IRS. Your bank will send a 1099-INT for any year you earn $10 or more. On $10,000 at 4.50% APY, you'd owe tax on approximately $450. A high-yield savings account is not a tax-advantaged vehicle — if tax efficiency matters, consider inflation-indexed U.S. savings bonds or a high-yield money market inside a brokerage account.

faqs.q: How long does an ACH transfer take from a high-yield savings account?
faqs.a: External ACH transfers at all five banks fall in the standard one-to-three business day range, and none of them advertise same-day external delivery. Most banks post same-day or next-day for transfers within their own ecosystem. Large outgoing transfers (above $25K at some banks) may require a phone verification step that adds a day.

faqs.q: Do any of these savings accounts have withdrawal limits?
faqs.a: The federal 6-withdrawal-per-month limit (Regulation D) was suspended in 2020 and most banks no longer enforce it strictly. However, Synchrony still lists a 6-transaction guideline in their terms. Ally, Marcus, Wealthfront, and Capital One 360 allow unlimited withdrawals, though Wealthfront may flag large or frequent wire transfers for manual review.

faqs.q: Can I open a high-yield savings account if I already have one elsewhere?
faqs.a: Yes. There's no restriction on holding multiple savings accounts across banks. Many people keep their primary spending in one bank and park their emergency fund or short-term savings at a higher-yield online bank. The IRS has no limit on the number of accounts; the only limit is FDIC coverage per institution, so if your balance exceeds $250K at one bank, spreading across multiple institutions protects the full amount.

Wealthfront Corp. is an SEC-registered investment adviser, not a bank itself. The Cash Account is a brokerage product whose uninvested cash is swept into FDIC-insured partner banks through Green Dot Bank's network. Your money is insured — just through a different mechanism than a direct-bank account. Wealthfront's investing side is separate and SIPC-protected.

faqs.q: What is the minimum deposit to open these accounts?
faqs.a: Ally, Marcus, Synchrony, and Capital One 360 all require $0 to open — you can start with any amount. Wealthfront requires $1 to activate the Cash Account (technically $0 to open, but $1 to actually earn interest). None of the five charge monthly maintenance fees regardless of balance.

faqs.q: Which bank has the best mobile app for savings management?
faqs.a: Ally's app stood out for features — Savings Buckets and Boosters are genuinely useful for goal-based saving. Capital One's app has the slickest visual design and the tightest integration with checking and credit card accounts. Marcus and Wealthfront have functional but minimal apps. Synchrony's app is the weakest in terms of design and navigation.

faqs.q: How does compound interest work in a savings account?
faqs.a: High-yield savings accounts typically compound daily and pay interest monthly. On $10,000 at 4.50% APY: year 1 earnings are approximately $450. With daily compounding, you earn slightly more than the simple rate because each day's interest is added to the principal before the next day's interest is calculated. After 5 years at a steady 4.50%, $10,000 grows to roughly $12,462 — assuming the rate holds, which it won't.

offerNotes.ally-bank-savings: No fees, no minimum balance; Savings Buckets let you set named goals within one account; 24/7 phone support; APY 4.20%.
offerNotes.marcus-by-goldman-savings: Cleanest product in the group — one rate (4.40% APY), no fees, no minimum, no frills; backed by Goldman Sachs since 2016.
offerNotes.wealthfront-cash-account: Highest APY in the group at 4.50%; FDIC coverage up to $8M via 32-bank sweep; requires a Wealthfront brokerage account to open.
offerNotes.synchrony-bank-hys: 4.35% APY with an optional ATM card and nationwide fee rebates — the only account here that gives physical cash access without a separate checking account.
offerNotes.capital-one-360-performance-savings: 4.30% APY; the only top-5 HYSA with physical Cafe branch locations in 12+ US cities; instant transfers within Capital One ecosystem.

pinDescription: Top 5 high-yield savings accounts 2026: earn up to 4.50% APY with $0 fees — Ally vs Marcus vs Wealthfront vs Synchrony vs Capital One 360 compared.
